thread:
karen: FYI CS is getting multiple customer reports of 503s (~20% p95) starting ~08:30 UTC. Affected tenant: acme-corp. Customers say repeated timeouts and retries causing billing spikes.
jamie: On it. Do we have any worker restarts around that time?
pooja: looking at upstream logs — lots of `SIGSEGV` entries from infer-worker and NVML reports `GPU reset` on gpu-2.
ryan: stack traces? any mention of OOM or CUDA assertions?
pooja: short snippet from /var/log/upstream/infer-logs.log: ```
[08:30:12] infer-worker[pid:2411] ERROR: segfault at 0x7ff.. ip 0x55d3c2ab
[08:30:12] infer-worker[pid:2411] signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7ff
NVML: Device 2 reset detected
```
jamie: that looks like segfault concurrent with NVML reset — could be hardware or a buggy kernel path during large KV prefetch. Any pattern on request shapes?
pooja: yes — most impacted requests are toolcall-heavy with long embedding inputs and simultaneous auth retries. Batch sizes spiking to 64 under p99.
cs-oncall: Acme says it started after they ramped a burst of auth requests at 08:28 — they provided a sample request ID: rq_9f3b.
ryan: Can someone grab the infer-worker core dump and GPU logs from the node? Command: `sudo journalctl -u infer-worker -o short-iso --since "2025-08-10 08:25" > /tmp/trace.log`
pooja: grabbed logs and uploaded to /mnt/s3/triage/8765432101/trace.log
infra-bot: uploaded /mnt/s3/triage/8765432101/trace.log (sha256: a3f1...)
jamie: repro hypothesis — race between KV prefetch and model swap under priority toolcall backlog causing memory corruption -> GPU driver reset -> segfault. Plan: 1) cordon node and drain 2) roll infer-worker with kernel debug flags 3) throttle acme traffic via rate-limit fallback.
karen: CS wants mitigation ASAP — can we enable fallback routing to a lower-priority model for acme while we triage? This reduces billing but restores availability.
ryan: I'll push a routing rule now: `redwoodctl route update --tenant acme-corp --policy fallback:model-small --ttl 600`
pooja: applied. Confirming reduced error rate on metrics. p95 503s dropped from 20% -> 2% within 2 minutes.
cs-oncall: let customer know we routed to fallback model and we're investigating root cause. Karen please send update.
karen: on it — message sent: "We've routed you to a lower-throughput model to restore availability while we investigate. Engineering is triaging logs and core dumps."
jamie: for repro — steps we have so far: 1) Have acme run a burst of authenticated toolcalls (concurrent QPS > 400) with large embedding payloads (avg tokens ~6000) 2) Observe device memory climb on gpu-2 3) observe NVML reset + infer-worker segfault.
ryan: I've requested a gcc debug build to include ASAN-like checks in the serving binary and scheduled rolling deploy to a canary pool.
pooja: attached stack frame excerpt for the segfault: ```
#0 0x55d3c2ab in kv_prefetch::handle() at kv_prefetch.cpp:412
#1 0x55d4f8b2 in model_swap::apply() at model_swap.cpp:210
#2 0x55d5aef1 in infer_loop::process() at infer_loop.cpp:125
```
jamie: adding label: suspected-kv-prefetch-corruption. Assigning owners: jamie (SRE) + ryan (runtime). ETA initial root cause 6h.
cs-oncall: customer asked for ETA and whether refunds will be issued. Karen will coordinate billing.
karen: billing note: capture affected request IDs and totals; we've opened internal billing ticket BT-3421.
ryan: quick mitigation checkboxes: - [x] fallback routing applied - [x] cordon problematic host - [ ] collect full core dump (in progress) - [ ] reproduce in canary - [ ] rollback quantization change if repro'd
pooja: core dump saved at /mnt/s3/triage/8765432101/core-infer-2411.dmp, nvml logs at nvml-8765432101.tar.gz
jamie: next immediate action: collect reproducer from acme (we asked them to run a controlled burst with sample payloads), and I'll attach node telemetry dump. Also posting triage doc link: https://redwood.internal/triage/8765432101
cs-oncall: customer updated: they see degraded but usable service, appreciate the quick fallback.
karen: rounding up — will post incident summary once SRE has root cause. For now status: mitigated (fallback routing), investigating (segfault + GPU reset), owners assigned. :white_check_mark:
